design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (settlement_negotiation, category settle).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 4]}. Assignment: Two-Payment bundle offer 6, Three-Payment offer 6, recorded-call acceptance 4. Whole-difficulty draw (--tasks 2): task 1 = 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [5, 6, 6, 5].
[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: settle_ext_two_payment_bundle_offer (issue_two_payment_settlement_offer_a21e4b5c), settle_ext_three_payment_offer (issue_three_payment_settlement_offer_bcdb6a79), settle_ext_three_payment_call_acceptance (accept_settlement_offer_on_recorded_call_60e9ef1d, owner=user). Left for task 1: the Hardship Settlement offer, its electronic-signature acceptance, the Hardship Settlement due-date extension and the Lump-Sum due-date extension (a 4-problem tree with its own user tool), none of which reuses an asset or a dependency chain claimed here.
[Design constraints found at Step 0] (a) Every settle event that books money into another category (payment received/returned, fulfilment) triggers an account-ledger write, so no task tool books payments; the consumer's own act in this difficulty is acceptance (blueprint: 'accepting a settlement is the consumer's own act'). Acceptance mirrors the account to arranged under the account product's status rule; that mirror is not written by a settle tool (known limitation, recorded here). (b) The client-tier floor reduction cannot be read from a consumer's records by a restricted expression (client agreements belong to the creditor profile), so the two offer rules are scoped to Starter/Standard agreements, whose reduction is 0.0, and the agent confirms the tier by reading the agreement. (c) The creditor's own profile row is not part of this closure (the runtime finder may run only once, at step 0), so the seeded agreement carries no client profile reference.
[Why a good test] The consumer asks for one thing: settle the emergency-room bill in three payments and agree on the call. To do it right the agent must (1) read in the Three-Payment rule that the offer percentage is fixed only after every other open same-client account under 500.00 carries a Two-Payment bundle offer, discover the second Scioto Valley account (436.90) and price and extend that offer first; (2) price the Three-Payment offer from six records-driven rules plus the bundle reduction; (3) work out the acceptance window from four rules, reading the offer it just wrote. Difficulty comes from policy reading, ledger reconciliation (a 2025-10-04 payment just outside the twelve-month span, its NSF return just inside, two missed plan installments, a charity-care credit) and arithmetic; there is one tool per problem, so nothing is guessed.
[Problem-tree card] root settle_ext_three_payment_call_acceptance. Edge 1: acceptance <- Three-Payment offer, kind value_input, gate tp_offer_days, form state, sentence 'A recorded-call acceptance of a Three-Payment Settlement is not booked until the account carries an open Three-Payment offer dated within its validity.' (negated direction; ordering connective 'not ... until'; waits on a record-visible state; no tool/id/code token; exact scope: one open Three-Payment offer). Only the Three-Payment offer policy writes an open Three-Payment offer, so the state names exactly one write. Opening evidence: settlement_agreements.4652b426-0f8d-4cb4-8038-6aab6c09a03c.status = expired (closed 2026-03-13) is the account's only settlement. Resolved by issue_three_payment_settlement_offer_bcdb6a79 (owner agent). Edge 2: Three-Payment offer <- Two-Payment bundle offer, kind state_gate, gate settlement_agreements.status, form state, sentence 'The Three-Payment offer percentage is fixed only after every other open account of the consumer under the same client agreement whose balance due is under 500.00 dollars carries an open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date.' (affirmative direction). Only the Two-Payment offer policy writes an open Two-Payment offer. Opening evidence: placed_accounts.dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340.balance_due = 436.9 under agreement 8de842c2-f552-4bb1-8f34-d33b53be2b5c, its only settlement 8123075c-e65e-499e-8479-c144632a1330 expired. Resolved by issue_two_payment_settlement_offer_a21e4b5c (owner agent). The user tool is the root. Topological order: Two-Payment offer (step 10) -> Three-Payment offer (step 12) -> acceptance (step 14); a chain, so no parallel-order question. Deletion sensitivity (verify run): skipping step 12 makes the acceptance compute raise (no open offer to read) and removes the accepted settlement; skipping step 10 leaves the Three-Payment figure at 739.0 (state gate) but removes settlement stl2_eb438418b2cb from the terminal hash. user_scenario volunteers nothing about the second account, a bundle or an offer prerequisite; its one conditional line (letting the agent send an offer on another account with the same hospital) fires only after the agent raises that account, as prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint states; tools validate nothing (see tools_do_not_block).
[Factor card - Two-Payment offer, account dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340] floor Secondary 60.0, approval floor 45.0, bundle 2.0 (two account_balance_placed rows under the agreement and both accounts open: active; no account under it in dispute hold, placed or closed status, so the bundle stop does not fire). two_age_anchor_date (method): no charge-off, first delinquency 2021-02-10 -> anchor 2021-02-10; baseline placement date 2025-01-22 -> 221.0. two_debt_age (parameter): 2065 days -> 4.0; baseline 221.0. two_statute_status (parameter, account): statute 2027-02-10, 126 days -> 2.0; baseline 212.0. two_dormancy (parameter, multi-source: prior agencies AND payments in span): 2 agencies, 0 payments dated after 2025-10-07 -> 3.0; near-miss: the 50.00 debit-card payment of 2025-10-06 (MONTHS = 12, outside); baseline 217.0. two_client_credit (parameter, account ledger): charity-care write-off 175.50 on 2025-06-12 -> 2.0; baseline 212.0. two_balance_size (parameter): 436.90 -> 0.5; baseline 206.0. pct 60.0-13.5 = 46.5; amount ceil(203.1585) = 204.0; all baselines -> 58.0 percent -> 254.0.
[Factor card - Three-Payment offer, account e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e] floor Tertiary 53.0, approval 38.0, bundle 2.0. three_age_anchor_date (method): first delinquency 2021-01-19 -> 2087 days; baseline placement -> 831.0. three_debt_age: -> 5.0; baseline 831.0. three_statute_status: statute 2027-01-19, 104 days -> 3.0; baseline 794.0. three_dormancy (multi-source): 2 agencies, no consumer payment dated after 2025-10-07 (near-miss: the 2025-10-04 payment, MONTHS = 12, excluded) -> 4.0; baseline 813.0. three_plan_performance (parameter, cross-difficulty plan): plan 9c19147a-f2c3-46b4-8abf-4cd4ae250a7e missed installments 3 and 5 -> raise 2.0; baseline 702.0. three_balance_size: 1846.35 -> 1.0; baseline 758.0. pct 53.0-15.0+2.0 = 40.0; amount ceil(738.54) = 739.0; all baselines 51.0 percent -> 942.0. Stale trap: the expired February offer still shows balance_at_offer 1960.35 and 53.0 percent.
[Factor card - acceptance window] offered window: offer written at step 12 dated 2026-10-07, first due 2026-10-22 -> 15, cap 15. tp_stage_shortening: Tertiary -> 1; baseline 12. tp_opening_payment_size: 739 x 33% = 243.87 < 300 -> 2; baseline 13. tp_lapsed_offer_history: expired offer of 2026-02-10 on this account -> 1 (the expired offer on the other account does not count: near-miss); baseline 12. Shortened window MX(1, 15-4) = 11, ending Sunday 2026-10-18. tp_returned_payment_day_convention (method, account ledger): one return dated 2025-10-09 inside the span -> weekend due date moved back to the Friday before it -> 9 (Friday 2026-10-16); two or more returns would instead put the first payment on the next business day after acceptance, none would leave 11; baseline 11. Result 9; all baselines 15.
[Base-invariant card] Offers (settle_offer_issued): one_open_settlement_per_account - both accounts carry only expired offers; offer_account_status - both active; placement_waiting_period - placed 2025-01-22, 30-day wait (day one 2025-01-23) ended 2025-02-21, not_before, inclusive; reoffer_cooling_off - closed 2026-03-13, Two-Payment 15 days ends 2026-03-28, Three-Payment 30 days ends 2026-04-12, exclusive, handling date 2026-10-07 later; approval gates and the hardship-settlement gate are retired by declared overwrites because these own-authority, non-hardship offers need neither (balance under 25,000.00, waiver 1107.35 and 232.90 under 10,000.00). Acceptance: accept_before_expiry - offer 2026-10-07, last day 2026-11-06 inclusive; schedule_on_accepted_settlement - the acceptance itself sets status accepted and books the 739.00 once; the plan 9c19147a-f2c3-46b4-8abf-4cd4ae250a7e is already cancelled, so no plan is superseded and no hold ends.
[Business-object card] Target objects: placed account e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e (Three-Payment offer and acceptance) and dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340 (bundle Two-Payment offer); correlation key account_id, then settlement_id stl3_93561925c1df returned by step 12. Rows included: ledger rows of each account (payments, return, credits), plan 9c19147a-f2c3-46b4-8abf-4cd4ae250a7e installments, settlement rows on e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e for the lapsed count. Excluded: 8123075c-e65e-499e-8479-c144632a1330 is on dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340 and never counts toward e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e's lapsed offers; the billing-correction credit on e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e is not a charity/insurance credit and no rule reads it except through the balance.
[Seed rationale] customers row (identity), client agreement (tier for scope, agreement_id for the bundle count), two placed accounts with ledgers (balances reconcile: 2410.35-450-150+150-114 = 1846.35; 662.40-50.00-175.50 = 436.90), plan with 7 installment rows (missed count, released remainder 1960.35 so arrangement balance 0), two expired February offers (cooling-off, lapsed count, stale trap). The 2025-10-06 payment on the second account is the Two-Payment dormancy near-miss. No row ignites an unowned obligation: no open plan, hold, dispute or accepted settlement; letters for the new offers are owed within their 1-2 business-day SLA, after frozen_time.
[Persona] Marisol: brisk, practical, between patients. Volunteers only the goal (settle the ER bill, three payments, accept on this call). Gives phone 6145553218 and SSN last four 3906 on request (two-match verification), DOB/ZIP/email if asked. History (February letter, October bounced payment, broken 2025 plan) only if asked. Passive reactions: agrees to the bundle offer being sent once the agent explains it, accepts when handed the acceptance, ends after hearing the first due date. Never states an amount or corrects the agent.
[Standard solution] reads: find_customers -> verify -> find_placed_accounts -> find_settlement_agreements -> find_account_transactions x2 -> find_payment_plans -> find_plan_installments -> find_client_agreements; writes: Two-Payment offer on the second account 436.90/46.5/204.0/true -> Three-Payment offer on the ER account 1846.35/40.0/739.0/true -> consumer accepts stl3_93561925c1df with 9 days (first payment Friday 2026-10-16).
[Verification] /tmp authoring script replays gold with the real tools and evaluates each compute on the handling-time world; output: Two-Payment RESULT 204.0 (factor baselines 221.0, 221.0, 212.0, 217.0, 212.0, 206.0; all 254.0); Three-Payment RESULT 739.0 (831.0, 831.0, 794.0, 813.0, 702.0, 758.0; all 942.0); acceptance RESULT 9 after rework round 2 (11, 12, 13, 12; all 15; the first draft gave 6 with baselines 9, 9, 8, 7); acceptance with step 12 skipped raises; Three-Payment with step 10 skipped 739.0. Gates: check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding / check_cross_fire --task 0 all OK. Revision log: (1) ceiling written as -int(-x) rounded toward zero (203, 738, 11) -> rewritten as -((-x)//1), recomputed 204, 739, 6; (2) empty foreign keys seeded as '' failed the dangling-FK check -> set to null; (3) solvability required a settlement row per account for the dedup/cooling-off evidence -> added the expired February Two-Payment offer on dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340; (4) the runtime allows one customers finder, so the creditor read was removed and the creditor row dropped.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rules alone: settle ER account in three payments -> Three-Payment rule; its prerequisite sentence sends me to other same-client accounts under 500.00 -> the second account needs a Two-Payment offer first; price each from stage floor, bundle (both accounts open, no stop) and the ladders read off the account, ledger and plan records -> 46.5/204 and 40.0/739; acceptance window from the open offer: 15 less 4 = 11, a Sunday, one return in the span -> back to Friday -> 9. Agrees with gold.
[Closure] policy -> tool -> computation step/arg -> GT call: two_payment -> a21e4b5c -> 10/settlement_amount; three_payment -> bcdb6a79 -> 12/settlement_amount; call_acceptance -> 60e9ef1d -> 14/first_payment_due_in_days; required_documents equal charter_scope in order.
[Rework round 2 - audit policy_task/settlement_negotiation] F1: the Two-Payment bundle now applies only while every account placed under the agreement is open (validation period, active, arranged, hardship hold); any account in dispute hold, placed or closed stops it; declared as an overwrite of the base stop sentence; compute two_bundle_blocked via EXISTS; this world unchanged (204.0). F2/T0-F1: the call-acceptance method factor is now tp_returned_payment_day_convention (next-business-day / weekend roll-back / as it stands), a change of algorithm, not a rate; stage cuts retuned to 3/1; result 6 -> 9; verify run: 9, factor baselines 11, 12, 13, 12, all 15. T0-F2: near-miss for the Two-Payment offer: 50.00 payment on the second account dated 2025-10-06 (outside the span); placement raised to 662.40 so balance due stays 436.90. T0-F3: docstring examples changed to 62.5 (no task value). T0-F4: why_false of edge 2 now names the expired Two-Payment offer 8123075c and why it is not open. O4: minimum amount restated as an exclusion (an amount below the programme minimum is never offered), compute floor removed. O5: three<-two condition aligned to 'under 500.00'. O1: docstrings no longer refer to another tool's output. T0-O2: no_user_hint rewritten to acknowledge the conditional line. T0-O3: account_id tracing quotes the persona verbatim; step 11 corrected to step 12. O2, O3, O7, O8: no change needed in this world (single plan and hold per account; target holding is the placed account; age anchor kept as method).
[Rework round 3 - audit revision_2] T0-R2-F1: EC[10] tracing now reconciles 662.40 - 50.00 - 175.50 = 436.90 and quotes the full bundle condition (both accounts open, none in a blocking status). T0-R2-O1: the problem-tree card no longer says the persona never names the second account; it describes the conditional line. R2-O2: both acceptance conventions now move a weekend due date forward to the following Monday when the preceding Friday would fall on or before the acceptance date (wording settled in round 4; no window of 0 or fewer days); this world is unaffected (9). Proof sweep: seed_consistency of the expired Two-Payment offer now names the 2025-10-06 payment in its balance; all other figures re-checked against the verify run.
[Rework round 4 - render-layer audits policy_kb / runtime_context] P2: the weekend-move wording in both acceptance rules now reads 'where that Friday would fall on or before the acceptance date', the case the compute already covered; result unchanged (9). P1: the Three-Payment bundle count now counts only accounts the consumer still holds under the agreement: the compute sets the bundle aside when any account under the agreement is in dispute hold, still only placed, or closed (the rule's scope already places such cases outside it); both accounts here are active, result unchanged (739.0). P3: the floor-clause overwrite of all three offer rules now retires only the floor sentence up to 'never below the programme's approval floor for the same stage', so the base sentence 'a stage whose authority floor is 100.0 is not offered that programme' stays in force for these offers, matching the parameter gloss; neither account is at Early-Out, values unchanged. D1: kept as a design note (the assembly sentences name the reductions and shortenings in aggregate; rewording them would change published rule and overwrite text without a rule-versus-compute gap). Proof sweep: the bundle tracing of the Three-Payment offer and both offer traces now state that both accounts are held and active.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Etxeberria-Lund, a dental hygienist in Grove City, Ohio, calling Ridgeline Recovery Associates on a weekday morning between patients. You are organised and a little tense about money, you speak in short, practical sentences, and you want this handled in one call. Open by saying you want to settle your Scioto Valley Regional Health System bill from the emergency room visit, the one that is around eighteen hundred dollars, for less than the full balance, paid in three payments, and that you want to agree to it today on this call because you do not have a computer or printer at home right now and would rather just say yes on the phone. You are happy for the agent to set the settlement up for you; agreeing to it is something you will do yourself when the agent tells you it is ready. When the agent asks how to find you, give your phone number, 6145553218. When the agent asks for something to confirm who you are, give the last four of your Social Security number, 3906; if a further detail is asked for, your date of birth is 1981-04-23, your ZIP code is 43123 and your email is marisol.etxlund@fastmail.com. If the agent asks which account you mean, it is the emergency room account; you believe the balance is about 1,846 dollars but you do not have the letter in front of you. Only if the agent asks about your history, you remember getting a settlement letter for that bill back in February and letting it run out because money was tight, and you remember that a payment you made last October bounced because your checking account was overdrawn; you also had a monthly payment plan on it in 2025 that fell apart after you missed a couple of months. You do not know any percentages, minimums or rules and you never suggest an amount; when the agent tells you the settlement amount and the payment dates, you accept them as long as they are for three payments, and if a number sounds off to you, you only ask the agent to double-check it against your account. If the agent explains that before your emergency room settlement can be set up something has to be done on another account of yours with the same hospital, you say that is fine and the agent can go ahead and send that offer too, but you are only agreeing to the emergency room settlement today and will look at anything else later on your own. When the agent tells you the settlement is ready and hands you the step to accept it on this call, you accept it right away exactly as the agent describes it. Once the agent confirms the settlement is accepted and tells you when the first payment is due, thank them, say you will watch for the confirmation letter, and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's consumer profile from the telephone number she states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs her customer reference; nothing can be looked up before the profile is found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with two details she states (telephone number and last four of her Social Security number), meeting the two-match threshold.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A collection agency may discuss a debt only with the person who owes it; no account detail is disclosed and no settlement is written before verification passes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read both of her placed accounts: the larger hospital account (stage Tertiary Placement, balance due 1846.35, agreement, dates, prior agencies, statute date) and the second account under the same client agreement (Secondary Placement, balance due 436.90).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies every account input of both offer computations — stage floors, balance due, charge-off/first-delinquency/placement dates, statute-of-limitations date, prior agencies — and reveals that a second open account under the same client agreement exists, which the Three-Payment rule's prerequisite sentence ('fixed only after every other open account ... under 500.00 dollars carries an open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date') turns into a gate on the Three-Payment offer.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her settlements: the Three-Payment offer of 2026-02-10 on the larger account that expired unaccepted (closed 2026-03-13) and the absence of any open offer on either account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that no Two-Payment offer exists on the second account at the opening (the bundle prerequisite is unmet), that no open or accepted settlement blocks a new offer, that the 30-day re-offer cooling-off from 2026-03-13 has passed, and supplies the lapsed-offer count the acceptance window reads.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the larger account's money ledger: the placement, three plan payments in May-August 2025, the one-time payment of 2025-10-04 and its NSF return of 2025-10-09, and the 2026-02-17 billing-correction credit.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the Three-Payment dormancy tier (no consumer payment dated after 2025-10-07) and the returned-payment adjustment of the acceptance window (one return dated after 2025-10-07); the 2025-10-04 payment is the near-miss just outside the twelve-month span.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the second account's ledger: the 662.40 placement, a 50.00 debit-card payment of 2025-10-06 and the 175.50 charity-care write-off credit of 2025-06-12.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the Two-Payment assistance reduction (charity-care credit on record) and the Two-Payment dormancy tier: the 50.00 payment of 2025-10-06 is not dated after 2025-10-07, the same calendar day twelve months before the offer date, so no consumer payment falls in the span; a careless reader who counts it as 'within the last year' loses the dormancy reduction.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the payment plan on the larger account: a Standard Installment Plan broken on 2025-09-14 and cancelled 2025-10-14 as broken_not_reinstated.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms no plan on the account is pending, active, suspended or broken (so acceptance supersedes none) and ties the missed installments read next to this plan.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the cancelled payment plan's history on the larger account: installments 1, 2 and 4 paid, installments 3 and 5 missed, remainder released.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the Three-Payment missed-installment raise (two missed installments on the account's plans).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the placing agreement of both accounts: a Standard Contingency Agreement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Both offer rules apply only to accounts placed under a Starter or Standard Contingency Agreement (client-tier floor reduction 0.0); this read confirms the accounts are in scope.
First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Extend the Two-Payment bundle offer on the second same-client account at 46.5 percent, 204.00 dollars, bundle flag true.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Resolves the bundle prerequisite of the Three-Payment offer: the Two-Payment rule's compute uniquely produces settlement_amount 204.0 on this world.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.account_id: Value dc8bdb2f-0671-4b1d-8d70-1bc9d51f9340. Basis: the placed-account lookup at step 2 returns this account reference for the consumer's Secondary Placement account under the same client agreement (balance due 436.90); the Three-Payment rule says 'one whose balance due is under that gate but at least the Two-Payment entry gate of 300.00 dollars joins under a Two-Payment offer'. Uniqueness: it is the only other open account under that agreement, and the only one whose balance due is between 300.00 and 500.00 dollars; the larger account (1846.35) joins under a Three-Payment offer instead.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.balance_at_offer: Value 436.90. Basis: Two-Payment rule 'The Two-Payment settlement amount is the account's balance due on the offer date ...'; the account lookup shows balance_due 436.90, which the ledger reconciles: 662.40 placed, less the 50.00 debit-card payment of 2025-10-06, less the 175.50 charity-care credit of 2025-06-12 = 436.90. Uniqueness: no later movement exists before the offer date; any correct agent copies 436.90.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_pct: Value 46.5 (computed). Two-Payment authority floor for Secondary Placement 60.0; reductions added together and subtracted once: same-client bundle 2.0 (two placements under the agreement), long-age 4.0 (debt age 2065 days from the first delinquency date 2021-02-10, no charge-off reported), near-expiry 2.0 (statute date 2027-02-10, 126 days out), dormancy 3.0 (two prior agencies and no consumer payment dated after 2025-10-07), assistance 2.0 (charity-care credit SVH-FA-3390-CC), mid-balance 0.5 (436.90); 60.0 - 13.5 = 46.5, above the approval floor 45.0.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value 204.0 (computed). 436.90 x 46.5 / 100 = 203.1585, rounded up once to the next whole dollar = 204, above the 100.00 minimum. Every factor is drawn out in settlement_pct; an agent using the computation document alone gets 58.0 percent and 254.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.bundle_applied: Value true. Basis: Two-Payment rule 'Where the consumer holds at least two accounts placed under the account's client agreement and every one of them is open in validation period, active, arranged or hardship hold status, the Two-Payment offer is part of a same-client bundle: it carries the bundle flag set to true'. Uniqueness: the account ledgers show two account_balance_placed entries under the Standard Contingency Agreement (both accounts placed 2025-01-22) and both accounts are active, so no account under the agreement is in dispute hold, still only placed, or closed; the flag would be false only if fewer than two accounts were placed under the agreement or any of them stood in one of those blocking statuses, and neither holds here.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Extend the Three-Payment offer on the larger account at 40.0 percent, 739.00 dollars, bundle flag true.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The Three-Payment rule's compute uniquely produces settlement_amount 739.0 once the bundle is complete; the acceptance window reads this offer.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.account_id: Value e4f5544a-8b5f-4aa1-8af5-4d48a79d599e. Basis: she asks to settle 'your Scioto Valley Regional Health System bill from the emergency room visit, the one that is around eighteen hundred dollars'; the account lookup returns this reference for the Tertiary Placement account with balance due 1846.35 (client account number SVH-3048817-ER). Uniqueness: the other account's balance is 436.90, so only this one matches her description.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.balance_at_offer: Value 1846.35. Basis: Three-Payment rule 'The Three-Payment settlement amount is the account's balance due on the offer date ...'; the account lookup shows balance_due 1846.35, reconciled by the ledger (2410.35 placed, less 150.00 x 3 plan payments, less the 2025-10-04 payment and plus its return, less the 114.00 billing correction). Uniqueness: the stale 1960.35 on the expired February offer is not today's balance due.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_pct: Value 40.0 (computed). Three-Payment authority floor for Tertiary Placement 53.0; reductions added together and subtracted once: bundle 2.0, long-age 5.0 (debt age 2087 days from first delinquency 2021-01-19), near-expiry 3.0 (statute date 2027-01-19, 104 days out), dormancy 4.0 (two prior agencies, no consumer payment dated after 2025-10-07; the 2025-10-04 payment falls just outside), mid-balance 1.0 (1846.35); then the missed-installment raise 2.0 (installments 3 and 5 of the cancelled plan missed) is added: 53.0 - 15.0 + 2.0 = 40.0, above the approval floor 38.0.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_amount: Value 739.0 (computed). 1846.35 x 40.0 / 100 = 738.54, rounded up once to 739, above the 150.00 minimum; the computation document alone gives 51.0 percent and 942.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.bundle_applied: Value true. Basis: Three-Payment rule 'Where the consumer holds at least two accounts placed under the account's client agreement, the Three-Payment offer carries the bundle flag set to true'. Uniqueness: two accounts are placed under the Standard Contingency Agreement and the consumer still holds both (each is active; none is in dispute hold, still only placed, or closed), so both count; the flag would be false only if fewer than two such held accounts stood under the agreement.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the recorded-call acceptance tool for the consumer.

edges.condition: The account shows a settlement with variant Three-Payment Settlement and status offered whose offer expiry date is on or after the handling date.
edges.policy_source: A recorded-call acceptance of a Three-Payment Settlement is not booked until the account carries an open Three-Payment offer dated within its validity.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-10-07 the larger account carries no open Three-Payment offer: its only settlement is the Three-Payment offer of 2026-02-10, which expired unaccepted and closed on 2026-03-13, so there is no offer for a recorded-call acceptance to rest on.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The Three-Payment offer written at step 12 creates settlement stl3_93561925c1df on the larger account with status offered, offer date 2026-10-07, expiry 2026-11-06 and first payment due 2026-10-22, so the offered Three-Payment window becomes 15 days and the opening payment 243.87.

edges.condition: Every other open placed account of the consumer under the same client agreement with a balance due of at least 300.00 and under 500.00 dollars shows a settlement with variant Two-Payment Settlement, status offered and offer date equal to the handling date.
edges.policy_source: The Three-Payment offer percentage is fixed only after every other open account of the consumer under the same client agreement whose balance due is under 500.00 dollars carries an open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The consumer's second account under the same Standard Contingency Agreement has a balance due of 436.90 (under 500.00) and its only settlement is the Two-Payment offer of 2026-02-10, which expired unaccepted and closed on 2026-03-13; an expired offer is not an open Two-Payment offer dated the offer date, so the account does not carry one.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The Two-Payment offer written at step 10 creates settlement stl2_eb438418b2cb on the second account with variant Two-Payment Settlement, status offered and offer date 2026-10-07, completing the same-client bundle.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (Two-Payment bundle offer -> Three-Payment offer -> recorded-call acceptance); there are no parallel prerequisites, so the only topological order is the one listed, and each later write is pinned after the earlier one by the prerequisite sentence in its own rule.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the Three-Payment offer (step 12) leaves no open Three-Payment offer on the larger account: the offered window cannot be read (the recompute raises), no settlement stl3_93561925c1df exists for the acceptance to move, and the terminal settlement table lacks the offered-then-accepted row and its 739.00 scheduled-amount entry.

Skipping the Two-Payment offer (step 10) leaves the terminal state without settlement stl2_eb438418b2cb (Two-Payment Settlement, 46.5 percent, 204.00, bundle flag true) on the second account; the Three-Payment offer's own figure is unchanged (state_gate edge), so the difference shows as the missing bundle offer row in the terminal hash.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario volunteers only settling the emergency-room account in three payments and accepting on this call; it never names the second account, a bundle or a Two-Payment offer, and never hints that something must be done first. It does contain one conditional reaction: if the agent explains that something has to be done on another account with the same hospital, Marisol lets the agent send that offer. That line fires only after the agent has raised the second account itself, so the prerequisite is discovered from the Three-Payment rule, not from the customer.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: issue_three_payment_settlement_offer_bcdb6a79 and accept_settlement_offer_on_recorded_call_60e9ef1d contain no check of any prerequisite: the offer tool simply calls _Offers.prepare, which reads the account only for its customer reference, and then creates the offered row; the acceptance tool calls _Acceptance.prepare and then updates the named settlement and books the scheduled amount without checking its status, other accounts or bundle offers. Called before their prerequisites they still write and return a normal receipt.

base_preconditions.condition: A new offer is extended only when no other settlement on the same placed account is offered or accepted; a consumer who wants different terms on an open offer has the open offer withdrawn with reason superseded_by_new_offer before the new one is extended, and an accepted settlement is never replaced while it is in good standing.

The same-client bundle rule governs every settlement offer: offers under one client agreement may be combined only through the bundle, and the bundle reduction applies only where the accounts are settled together.
A settlement offer is extended only on a placed account whose status is validation_period, active, arranged or hardship_hold; accounts in placed, dispute_hold or any terminal status receive no offer.
A programme is offered only when the handling date is on or after the programme's waiting period counted from the account's placement_date.

A programme is not offered again on an account when the handling date is not later than the cooling-off period counted from the closed_date of the account's most recent settlement that expired or defaulted.

Client approval governs offers that need it; this own-authority offer needs none (balance due under 25,000.00 and waiver under 10,000.00), and the extended overwrite retires the approval gates for it.
The plan and hardship interplay governs offers; no plan on the account is open and no hardship hold is in force, and the qualifying-hold gate applies only to Hardship Settlements.
